metadata.name: Corrected Sodium for Hyperglycemia (Katz Formula)
metadata.summary: Estimates true serum sodium in hyperglycemia using Katz's 1.6 mEq/L per 100 mg/dL correction factor.
clinical_pearls: No correction is added when serum glucose is <= 100 mg/dL (5.55 mmol/L).
For extreme hyperglycemia (> 400 mg/dL), compare with Hillier's 2.4 mEq/L per 100 mg/dL correction factor (Hillier et al., 1999).
Repeat serum sodium frequently during insulin and fluid therapy, as sodium shifts rapidly with glucose correction.

Pitfall — True hyponatremia & pseudohyponatremia: Extreme hyperglycemia can mask underlying true hypotonic hyponatremia (associated with worse outcomes), and an elevated osmolality gap should prompt screening for pseudohyponatremia.

interpretation.label: True Hyponatremia (< 135 mEq/L)
interpretation.summary: Corrected sodium remains below 135 mEq/L; evaluate true hypotonic hyponatremia.

interpretation.label: Normal Corrected Sodium (135–145 mEq/L)
interpretation.summary: Apparent hyponatremia is accounted for by hyperglycemic osmotic shift.

interpretation.label: Hypernatremia (> 145 mEq/L)
interpretation.summary: Free-water deficit present; monitor sodium closely during insulin/fluid therapy to avoid cerebral edema.

assessment_guides.title: Katz Formula Scope & Neuro-ICU Caveats
bedside_steps: Use contemporaneously drawn serum sodium and glucose values.
pitfalls_and_exceptions: Formula adds 1.6 mEq/L for each 100 mg/dL glucose above 100 mg/dL.
Rapid drops in corrected sodium (> 8–10 mEq/L/24h) during DKA/HHS treatment increase cerebral edema risk.

references.citation: Katz MA. Hyperglycemia-induced hyponatremia—calculation of expected serum sodium depression. N Engl J Med. 1973;289(16):843-844.
Hillier TA, Abbott RD, Barrett EJ. Hyponatremia: evaluating the correction factor for hyperglycemia. Am J Med. 1999;106(4):399-403.

Chuang C, Guo YW, Chen HS. Corrected sodium levels for hyperglycemia is a better predictor than measured sodium levels for clinical outcomes among patients with extreme hyperglycemia. J Chin Med Assoc. 2020;83(9):845-851.
